input: Find a grief counselor specializing in pregnancy loss

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing who the counseling is for (the user themselves, a partner, a couple together, or someone else) determines whether to look for individual, couples, or third-party referral options.
Whether the user wants in-person sessions or is open to telehealth changes which geographic area to search and how broad the options can be.
The specific type of loss (miscarriage, stillbirth, TFMR, infertility-related loss, etc.) affects which specializations or counselor backgrounds are most relevant.
Insurance coverage, out-of-pocket budget, or sliding-scale needs directly determine which counselors are financially accessible and worth pursuing.
The user's location (city, region, or country) is essential for surfacing relevant local or regional options.
Preferences around counselor background (e.g., gender, religious/secular approach, therapeutic modality like CBT or somatic therapy) affect fit and comfort.
Understanding what 'found' means to the user — a shortlist of names, a booked appointment, or a vetted recommendation — defines when this task is actually complete.

gold.taskTitle: Find a grief counselor for pregnancy loss
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to locate a grief counselor who specializes in pregnancy loss, which could involve miscarriage, stillbirth, or other forms of perinatal loss.

questions.title: Who is the counseling for — you, a partner, or both?
questions.description: Determine whether the user needs individual therapy, couples counseling, or is searching on behalf of someone else, so the right type of provider is targeted.

questions.title: What city or region should the search focus on?
questions.description: Establish the user's location to identify geographically relevant counselors and narrow the search appropriately.

questions.title: Do you prefer in-person sessions or is telehealth acceptable?
questions.description: Clarify the format preference so the search can include or exclude remote providers, which significantly widens or narrows the pool.

questions.title: What type of loss are you seeking support for?
questions.description: Identify whether the loss was a miscarriage, stillbirth, termination for medical reasons, or another form of perinatal loss, since some counselors specialize further within this field.

questions.title: Do you have insurance, or do you need a sliding-scale option?
questions.description: Understand the financial constraints so the search can filter for in-network providers, self-pay rates, or income-based sliding-scale counselors.

questions.title: Do you have preferences about the counselor's approach or background?
questions.description: Surface any preferences around therapeutic modality, counselor gender, or religious versus secular framing that would affect comfort and fit.

questions.title: What does success look like — a shortlist, or a booked appointment?
questions.description: Define the end goal so the plan can stop at a curated list of names, or extend to helping the user reach out and schedule a first session.
